result.rationale: The diff shows parseRefreshTokenResponse returns `refreshTokenResponse` — the full SafeParseReturnType ({success, data}) — while Google's CalendarService change does `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema); await prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, persisting the wrapper object as the credential key instead of `key.data`. Subsequent refreshes read `googleCredentials.access_token`/`expiry_date` from a malformed key, breaking token refresh; this is a verifiable correctness defect introduced by the diff.

judged_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper ({success, data}), but the Google CalendarService assigns that wrapper directly as the stored credential key (`data: { key }`) instead of `key.data`. After any token refresh, credential.key is persisted as {success:true,data:{...}} instead of the Google credential shape, so every subsequent Google API call reading key.access_token/key.expiry_date gets undefined and calendar sync breaks for that user.

After any token refresh, credential.key is persisted as {success:true,data:{...}} instead of the Google credential shape, so every subsequent Google API call reading key.access_token/key.expiry_date gets undefined and calendar sync breaks for that user.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (a `{ success, data }` wrapper) and throws if `!success`, but it still returns the wrapper rather than `data`. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refreshed credentials are parsed via `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persisted with `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, which would store the wrapper object instead of the Google credential shape. That would break later code expecting `credential.key.access_token` / `expiry_date`.
